Now open the most promising pages.Base64 PDF; decode and extract text.I found three new dated AI predictions from Pichai in 2024, all from December. The three fixed searches ran, so this was not a quiet year. Two come from his signed note in Google's Gemini 2.0 announcement (December 11), and one from his printed interview with Semafor (published December 12). None of them matches a claim on your recorded list.

- **Gemini 2.0 note:** In his signed section of the post, he says reasoning from Gemini 2.0 is being tested in AI Overviews "this week" and will roll out more broadly "early next year." He also says AI Overviews will keep reaching more countries and languages "over the next year." That post has a second section by Demis Hassabis and Koray Kavukcuoglu. Its line "Early next year, we'll expand Gemini 2.0 to more Google products" is theirs, not Pichai's, so I left it out.
- **Semafor interview:** He says that looking ahead into 2025, the models are already good enough to build many uses on, and "That progress is going to be very real." This is a mild prediction, so you may decide it's too weak to count. The Waymo "10 cities next year" line on that page is the interviewer's question, not his words.

Things I could not confirm or left out:
- **Not checked:** A CNBC report of Google's internal strategy meeting on December 18 says Pichai named scaling Gemini for consumers as "our biggest focus next year." The page would not open, and it reads more like a company plan than a prediction about AI. I also did not open his X posts or the DealBook coverage, so I have quoted none of them. I saw a line attributed to him from that meeting only on a site that collects quotes, so I did not use it.
- **Excluded:** In the July earnings call he said NVIDIA's Blackwell chips would come to Google Cloud in early 2025. That is a chip forecast, so it stays out.

The quoting on the July call PDF and the Gemini 2.0 post cost me two extra page openings because of a mistake in my own code. That left only six openings, so the Q1 and Q3 earnings calls, the I/O keynote and his Decoder and Bloomberg interviews were not checked. Two of the 12 searches were unused, since without page openings they could not add quotable text.
